title: Best-of-N Jailbreak Risk in Defer-to-Resample: A Replication on Open Models

original_idea.body: Reimplement a minimal defer-to-resample loop with two open models, sweep k from 1 to 16, and measure how monitor evasion grows with k against the 1-(1-p)^k prediction.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A safe-k upper bound for a leading control protocol (DTR) directly informs control-protocol design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Minimal DTR loop with two open models, sweep k; clear inherited methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped k-sweep dose-response curve with a fitted prediction.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, replication/third-party scrutiny of a control protocol, lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Two open models, modest sampling on single GPU/API.

novelty.reasoning: Best-of-N DTR evasion warned about in source papers; this is replication/quantification on open models.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The effect is warned about; the open-model dose-response quantification may be open.
